- When sentiment is negative (≤0) in the recent 3–5 days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥1) over 3+ days, model tends to overestimate future prices; apply a 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% in next 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- In 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 1–3% if sentiment is positive and price is trending down; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5% to offset.
